title: The Moon Garden Folds Its Petals

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [faint night wind rustling leaves] [softly] Imagine sitting in a garden that blooms only beneath the moon. You do not need to silence the world; simply let the garden meet it gently.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the furthest sound. A night flower receives it on one wide petal, then slowly folds the petal inward.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice nearer sounds... the room, your clothing, the breath. Another petal closes without rejecting anything it touched.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Behind closed eyes, colours and after-images may shimmer. Let them dim like greenhouse lamps switching off one row at a time.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel temperature along the skin. Imagine the garden drawing its delicate leaves closer, keeping warmth near the stem.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Taste and scent may be vivid, faint, or absent. Let those pathways curl inward like silver vines returning to a trellis.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now include the whole outer world as weather beyond a glass roof. It can continue while you rest beneath it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Turn toward an inner sensation: the pulse in a fingertip, movement in the belly, or the quiet weight of your hands.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If a strong sensation asks for attention, respond kindly. Pratyahara is not disappearance; it is choosing where to place the lantern.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest at the centre of the folded flower. Sounds and sensations remain at the edges, softened by layers of patient petals.
[soft, slow, warm voice] For a few breaths, enjoy the inward garden without trying to make it perfectly still.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let each petal open again. Hear the room, feel the air, and return carrying a little moonlit quiet inside.
